citation.title: Relationship between attachment site of tibialis anterior muscle and shape of tibia: anatomical study of cadavers
citation.journal: Journal of Foot and Ankle Research

accessMethod: Publisher-hosted open full-text HTML directly opened in the in-app browser; Methods and Results sections, figures/captions, and limitations were read. Search result used only for discovery.
sourceStatus: Version-of-record bibliographic metadata displayed by Springer Nature; no local copy downloaded.
studyDesignAndSample: Gross anatomical cadaver dissection study of 40 lower legs (20 male, 20 female) from 20 Japanese cadavers. No detected right-left difference for reported parameters.

locators.locator: Materials and Methods, paragraph beginning “Twenty Japanese cadavers”; dissection protocol and origin definition
locators.observed: The TA tendon was cut and turned laterally. Origin was defined where muscle fibers firmly adhered to bone cortex. Distal ends of anterior and posterior tibial attachment were marked A and P, measured along tibial length. These are longitudinal endpoint measurements, not a condylar footprint triangle map.

The authors report anterior TA fibers originating from the lateral condyle and anterior border of the tibia; posterior fibers originate from the anterolateral tibial surface and anterior interosseous membrane. Fig. 1 is a cadaver dissection view, not a transferable mesh coordinate/triangle dataset.

locators.locator: Discussion, paragraph comparing textbook extents; Fig. 2/Table 1
locators.observed: The reported 47.1% and 66.1% values refer to distal limits of anterior and posterior fiber attachment along proximal-to-distal tibial length; the study does not provide a lateral-condyle surface boundary for this project mesh.
Authors note a relatively small Japanese cadaver sample, age/demographic generalizability limits, and formalin fixation.

independentAnatomySupport: Supports the broad claim that anterior tibialis anterior fibers include an origin at the tibial lateral condyle. It helps distinguish this attachment from shaft and interosseous-membrane claims but does not identify exact lateral-condyle surface extent or BodyParts3D FJ3387 triangles/coordinates.

sourceSeparation.historicalClaim: Gray 20th US edition (1918), section 8c, subsection “The Tibialis anterior (Tibialis anticus)”, printed p. 480; the source was opened as Bartleby chapter text in the browser. The project registry identifies the editor/publisher/edition.
sourceSeparation.modernEvidence: Kimata et al. 2022 peer-reviewed cadaveric study, original publisher full text opened; not a terminology index.
sourceSeparation.searchIndex: Discovery aid only; final support taken from opened full-text source.
sourceSeparation.humanAnatomyReview: Not performed by a credentialed project anatomy reviewer; AI/browser source check is not human approval.

geometryHoldReason: The modern study maps gross origin and longitudinal distal endpoints, but does not bound the lateral-condyle footprint with coordinates or mesh triangles. The unmarked FJ3387 surface has no source-to-mesh landmark crosswalk. Do not trace a patch from viewport appearance or transfer population ratios to this single adult-male template mesh.
